input:
Two tangents to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 4 at the points A and B meet at the point P(-4,0). Then the area of the quadrilateral PAOB, O being the origin, is

Options:
A. 2sqrt(3) sq. units
B. 8sqrt(3) sq. units
C. 4sqrt(3) sq. units
D. 6sqrt(3) sq. units

phase_1_understand_the_problem.problem_restatement: Find area of quadrilateral formed by external point P, tangent points A and B, and center O of circle x^2+y^2=4.
phase_1_understand_the_problem.key_observation: PAOB is composed of two congruent right triangles PAO and PBO.

key_concepts: Length of tangent from external point

phase_3_plan_the_approach.strategy: Compute tangent length AP, area of one right triangle with OA, then double it.
logical_steps: Step 2: Find AP using tangent-length formula
Step 3: Compute area of triangle PAO

phase_5_verify_answer.verification: Both triangles PAO and PBO are congruent right triangles with area 2sqrt(3), so total is 4sqrt(3).
